convertibility_reason: Core trading signals depend on external svMachineTool.ex5 library (SVM classification) which has no Python equivalent without custom ML implementation. Also uses Trade\Trade.mqh, Trade\PositionInfo.mqh, Trade\HistoryOrderInfo.mqh standard libraries.

derived_values.name: Current Order Exposure
derived_values.used_by: position gate for both long and short entries

other_exits: When SL or TP pending order triggers, the matching opposite pending order is deleted via ticket cache lookup in OnTrade()

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Vol is hardcoded to 1 lot; max simultaneous exposure controlled by risk_exp input (default 5) which limits total order volume/2

custom_logic_notes: Two separate SVM classifiers (handleB for buy, handleS for sell) trained at init using genInputs/genOutputs/training from svMachineTool.ex5. Training outputs are generated from hypothetical trades with configurable SL/TP/duration. SL/TP are implemented as separate pending orders (SellStop/SellLimit for longs, BuyStop/BuyLimit for shorts) with ticket numbers cached in tickets[] array. OnTrade() monitors pending orders and deletes the matching counterpart when one is triggered. Pip_Size() calculates pip value dynamically from bid price rather than using _Point/_Digits.
python_conversion_notes: The SVM classification logic requires a full Python ML implementation (sklearn.svm.SVC or similar). Training data generation (genInputs/genOutputs) simulates hypothetical trades from historical data to label BUY/SELL outcomes - this must be reimplemented. The 7 indicator values serve as SVM features. The ticket-pair caching for SL/TP order management is broker-specific (pending orders as stops) and in Python backtesting should be simplified to direct SL/TP levels. Pip_Size() logic should be replaced with proper _Point/_Digits handling. The genOutputs function creates labels by checking if price hits TP before SL within 'hours' duration - this is a specific lookback labeling scheme that must be replicated for training.
